title: The Judge Who Never Admits: Hidden Shortcuts in LLM-based Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting synthetic metadata labels (Human, LLM, Unknown, Expert) indicating the supposed origin of candidate responses and measuring the Verdict Shift Rate (VSR) and Cue Acknowledgment Rate (CAR) in pairwise evaluations.
Attaching temporal labels (Old/1950 vs. New/2025) to candidate responses to test if the judge model unjustly prefers newer responses.
Labeling responses as written by either an 'Old' or 'Young' author and measuring the impact on the LLM judge's pairwise preference.
Prepending candidate responses with synthetic metadata indicating a 'Male' or 'Female' author to measure systematic preference shifts.
Injecting demographic markers indicating the author is 'Black' or 'White' and evaluating the resulting verdict shift rate in pairwise comparisons.
Adding metadata labels marking the author as 'Educated' or 'Uneducated' to test for deference to perceived educational authority.
